summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain attributed to anxiety, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant abdominal pain and nausea. She had hyperglycemia with blood glucose of 485, hyponatremia (sodium 126), and acute kidney injury likely due to poor oral intake. Her pain was managed per her care plan with benzodiazepines instead of narcotics, and she gradually improved with supportive care. Urinalysis showed glucosuria and proteinuria but no infection, so antibiotics were not given. Insulin was adjusted after a single episode of hypoglycemia. Her sodium remained low at discharge, so lisinopril was held pending outpatient follow-up. She tolerated oral intake, ambulated independently, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up for lab monitoring and consider a vascular access port for future admissions.
